jobs.description:
Who we are:

We're one of Europe's fastest-growing fintech companies – on a mission to create the world's most empowering way to pay.

We launched the product in 2020 and achieved double unicorn status, valued at $2 billion, and since then have taken on more than 6 million customers.

Our mission is to become the best way to pay for anything, anywhere and say goodbye to credit costs for everyone. This is huge. Want to join us?

About the role.

Zilch is looking for an experienced social media and content manager to help shape how we show up online. You’ll lead our LinkedIn presence and manage content for the company blog, turning company, product, partnership and customer stories into clear, engaging material.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll be well-connected across the business, find stories, plan what to share, write and edit content, publish it, and learn from how it performs. You’ll help Zilch build a consistent presence throughout the year, not just around major announcements, and support senior leaders to share their ideas and expertise.

LinkedIn experience is essential. The role also covers the company blog and may extend to other channels as Zilch’s needs and opportunities evolve. As a payments business, accuracy and good judgement matter: you’ll need to make complex topics easy to understand without losing the detail.

 

Day to day responsibilities.

  • Own the day-to-day running of Zilch’s LinkedIn presence, including the content plan, publishing schedule and performance reviews.

  • Translate Zilch’s communications objectives into editorial priorities and content plans, making day-to-day decisions within agreed messaging and approval guidelines.

  • Manage the company blog: develop story ideas, write and edit articles, coordinate contributions and keep content up to date.

  • Write and edit clear, engaging posts, explainers, customer and partner stories, and other content for social channels and the blog.

  • Find useful stories in Zilch’s products, partnerships, people and business updates, and work with colleagues to bring them to life.

  • Help senior leaders develop a confident, authentic voice on LinkedIn. This may include drafting posts, articles and commentary on their behalf.

  • Turn company announcements and business milestones into a range of useful content for the blog, LinkedIn and other relevant channels.

  • Work with design, video and other teams to create content in formats that suit the story and the audience.

  • Track what people respond to, report on results and use these insights to improve results against channel objectives and performance measures agreed with communications leadership.

  • Keep an eye on relevant conversations and trends, and bring forward timely ideas that fit Zilch.

  • You’ll sit within the communications team and work closely with Marketing, Product, Commercial and Legal teams to find stories, check facts and coordinate content.

  • Establish and improve editorial workflows, briefing and approval processes, and content standards, working with Legal and other teams to ensure accuracy and timely publication.

  • Guide colleagues who contribute content, sharing feedback and practical advice to strengthen writing quality and consistency.

  • Help develop Zilch’s presence on other channels where there is a good opportunity to reach the right audience. This could include existing or new social platforms, video, newsletters or other formats.

  • Develop relationships and support work with creators, influencers or finance voices when it fits a campaign.

 

What we’re looking for...

  • Around 5-10 years’ experience in social media, content or editorial roles.

  • Strong, hands-on experience managing and creating content for LinkedIn. You can show how you’ve built a consistent company or executive presence on the platform.

  • Excellent writing and editing skills, with examples of work that is clear, engaging and well judged.

  • The ability to explain financial, technical or regulatory topics in plain English while keeping them accurate.

  • A creative flair for developing great content and the ability to spot trends and jump on them early

  • Strong organisation skills and the ability to manage several pieces of work at once.

  • Confidence working with senior leaders and colleagues across different teams to find and develop stories.

  • The drive to make connections with finfluencers in the industry and collaborate

  • Experience with other social channels or content formats is useful, and you’re open to exploring new ones as Zilch’s needs develop.

A background in finance, fintech or technology would be preferable. Experience in another consumer-facing or regulated industry would also be relevant.

jobs.title: Ops Associate
jobs.description:
At Parallel, we build AI agents to help healthcare facilities automate their administrative processes and unlock additional revenue, starting with medical coding.


Today, up to 25% of healthcare spending is lost in manual, repetitive administrative work. Legacy software hasn’t helped, it’s made things slower, more complex, and more frustrating for care teams.

We believe AI agents can change that. Our technology combines Large Language Models with system-level automation to handle real work inside existing hospital tools. No integrations, no disruption.

Our first agent automates coding workflows and frees up time for medical staff to focus on patients.

We launched in 2024, are backed by top investors (Index, Frst, Y Combinator, Hexa, Kima Ventures, Better Angle), and we’re just getting started.

 

The future of healthcare isn’t just digital — it’s automated. Come help us build it !

The role

At Parallel, we work with a team of 25+ freelance TIMs (medical information technicians) on different tasks, in particular retrieving medical documents from our partner facilities’ software. This is a core part of Parallel. With fast, secure access to our partner facilities’ data, we code the first hospital stays within a few days and prove Parallel’s ROI. Then we automate document extraction so we can scale.

As Ops Associate, you support the Ops team on managing freelancers and on cross-functional Ops projects. You take ownership of critical operational topics end to end and contribute directly to Parallel’s growth. You work daily with our Head of Ops, the Deployment Strategists, Customer Care and our freelance TIMs.

You’re in charge of staffing and managing our network of freelance TIMs and become their main point of contact, working directly with our Head of Ops. You also work on cross-functional projects that structure Ops as Parallel scales. It’s a chance to see first-hand how a generative AI solution is deployed in hospitals, and to experience a startup’s scale-up from the inside.

What you’ll do

Staffing and management of freelance TIMs

You’re responsible for the network of freelance TIMs who support our clients. You make sure the right person is on the right assignment, at the right time, within a compliant framework.

  • Sourcing and recruiting: identify, qualify and recruit new TIMs based on needs (specialties, facilities, volume).

  • Staffing assignments: assign TIMs to client accounts, anticipate workload peaks and manage priorities.

  • Onboarding: train new TIMs on the Parallel tool and our ways of working.

  • Monitoring: centralize assignment tracking and manage the team’s performance.

  • Contracts and compliance: keep freelance contracts up to date, in line with our ISO 27001 and HDS requirements (data access, confidentiality).

Cross-functional Ops projects

You support the Ops team on cross-functional projects to make processes more robust and scalable. For example, you could:

  • Compliance and security: contribute to the ISO 27001 and HDS certification project on the Ops side (registers, evidence, access reviews, contracts).

  • Processes and documentation: keep client training notes up to date and improve internal playbooks (deployment, support).

Who we’re looking for

  • You’re looking for your first permanent job, or possibly an end-of-studies internship (with the goal of staying with us on a permanent contract).

  • You’re rigorous: you organize yourself, prioritize, and follow your topics through to the end.

  • You have strong people skills: you can adapt to profiles very different from yours, explain technical topics and bring a team along.

  • You’re comfortable in a tech environment and like understanding how software works so you can help others use it.

  • You’re autonomous: when you’re given an assignment, you figure out how to set up the right processes and resources to get it done.

Why join us?

  • Real impact: our agents free hospital teams from administrative work.

  • A central role: you work with Ops, Product, Tech and the field teams.

  • Room to grow: we’re hiring for this role to help someone grow with us over time.

  • The right time: Series A closed, product already used by ~100 hospitals, a fast-growing team.

  • The package: Alan health insurance, Swile, Apple equipment, 50% of transport covered, a team event every month and two off-sites a year.

  • Our offices: Paris 2nd arrondissement, boulevard de Sébastopol.

The process

  1. Call with Léa, Talent Lead (30 min)

  2. Call with Clémentine, Head of Ops and your future manager (30 min)

  3. Case study with Clémentine and Jules and meeting with Paul, CEO

  4. Offer

We care about who you are, not just what's on your CV.

If you're drawn to what we're building but don't meet every requirement, we still want to hear from you. Studies show that women in particular tend to apply only when they meet 100% of the criteria. If that's you, please don't let that hold you back. We'd love to receive your application.

jobs.title: Accounts Assistant
jobs.description:
💰 £40,000–£45,000

📍 Salary based on London. Other locations may vary.

Fanvue is one of the fastest-growing creator monetisation platforms globally. We're an AI-powered, creator-first platform helping creators connect, engage, and earn directly from their audiences at scale. Following our recent Series A, Fanvue has surpassed $200m+ in annual recurring revenue, with triple-digit year-on-year growth, supporting hundreds of thousands of creators and millions of fans worldwide.

Behind the product is a finance function that needs to be as fast and reliable as the platform itself.

🎯 The Role

We're hiring an Assistant Accountant to own the accounting engine of the finance team: the ledger, the month-end close, and the admin that keeps both clean. Our day-to-day transaction processing is supported by an outsourced bookkeeping partner. You'll own the quality of that work, the reconciliations behind it, and everything between a receipt landing and a number reaching the board pack.

Everything else in finance, reporting, forecasting and investor diligence depends on the ledger being right. You'll make sure it is: reviewing what goes in, reconciling what comes out, and closing the month on time. About a quarter of the role is finance admin. It means running the invoice inbox, chasing receipts and keeping supplier records clean, and it's what keeps the numbers right.

🚀 What You'll Do

Ledger and close

  • Review and own the ledger in Xero, including our outsourced bookkeepers' work on coding, supplier bills and daily bank reconciliations across GBP, USD and EUR accounts

  • Prepare month-end journals, accruals and prepayments, and the balance sheet reconciliations behind them, so we close by working day 5 with our Finance Manager

  • Keep intercompany balances with our US entity reconciled

  • Reconcile payroll, PAYE and pension control accounts to Rippling each month

  • Prepare the UK VAT return in Xero for review

  • Prepare year-end schedules and answer queries from our external accountants and auditors

Finance admin and communication

  • Run the invoice inbox, logging, chasing and routing supplier invoices so nothing reaches the ledger without a document

  • Chase receipts and missing context from colleagues for card spend, and keep receipt compliance high

  • Maintain supplier records and support onboarding, including verifying bank details before anything is paid

  • Be the first point of contact for finance questions from the wider team

👀 Who You Are

  • 2 to 4 years in a finance team or accounting practice, with at least one month-end close owned end to end

  • AAT qualified, or studying towards or part-qualified in ACCA, CIMA or ACA. We'll support your studies

  • Confident in Xero or similar cloud accounting software, and comfortable with large data sets in Excel or Google Sheets

  • Experience with multi-currency reconciliations and high transaction volumes

  • Clear, friendly written communication. You'll chase people across the company and keep it pleasant

  • Fintech, marketplace or payments experience is a strong plus

✨ You'll Thrive Here If

  • A fully reconciled balance sheet gives you real satisfaction

  • You chase people for answers instead of waiting

  • You see the admin as part of getting the numbers right, not a distraction from it

  • You're comfortable in a startup where things move fast around you, even if your work is methodical

  • You want to grow into a management accountant or financial controller role as the team scales

⚠️ You'll Struggle Here If

  • You want to work only on the numbers and see chasing colleagues for receipts as beneath the role

  • You need heavy supervision or detailed instructions for every task

  • You're not comfortable working with high transaction volumes daily

🌍 Why Join Fanvue?

  • Sunday Times Best Places to Work, two years running. We don't just say we have great culture, we prove it

  • Your work has immediate, visible impact. When the books are clean, the whole company moves faster, leadership gets reliable numbers, and investor conversations go smoothly

  • A clear path to grow, with study support and room to step up as the finance team expands

  • Fanvue supports hundreds of thousands of creators and millions of fans globally. The problems you solve here are real and immediate

  • Fully remote with unlimited PTO, flexible working hours, a London office and WeWork access when you want it

  • Salary reviews every six months, we don't wait for annual cycles to recognise your growth

  • Travel and office budgets for team off-sites or kitting out your home setup

  • A benefits package we're actively building out, including gym memberships and apps

  • A culture built on innovation, speed, excellence, ownership and transparency

⭐ Fanvue is for Everyone

We know that diverse teams build better products. Even if you do not meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. Potential, mindset, and ambition matter just as much as experience.

jobs.title: Operations Lead
jobs.description:
About Magentic

At Magentic, we're building the next generation of AI agents to transform how the world's largest companies manage procurement and supply chains.

We're tackling a $3 trillion market, building AI systems that can autonomously manage complex procurement workflows and help make global manufacturing supply chains more resilient.

Backed by Sequoia and Felicis, we've brought together an exceptional team with experience from OpenAI, Meta, Revolut, NASA and McKinsey.

We're growing quickly, solving challenging problems and building something with the potential to change how critical industries operate. It's an exciting time to join, early enough to make an huge impact and help shape what comes next.

About the Role

We're looking for an experienced Operations Lead to play a key role in shaping how Magentic operates as we grow.

This is the perfect opportunity for someone who is proactive, independent and comfortable taking ownership and making decisions. You'll be pragmatic and commercially minded, with a focus on delivering real impact rather than overcomplicating things. You'll thrive in a fast-paced startup environment, know how to balance competing priorities and be confident finding solutions that work for the business as we grow.

It’s a wide ranging, highly collaborative role that will interact with the whole business: you'll work across people operations, IT and tooling, legal and compliance, alongside leading projects that improve how we work across the business.

What You'll Do

  • Take ownership of key People Operations processes, helping create a great employee experience as we grow.

  • Shape how we use internal systems and tooling, finding smarter ways to work and opportunities to introduce automation.

  • Take ownership of legal and compliance operations, working with external advisers to ensure we're set up for success as we scale.

  • Drive high-impact projects, working closely with teams across the business to evolve our ways of working as we scale.

  • Build and introduce new processes that make a genuine difference to how we operate, bringing together people, tools and data to support our growth.

What We're Looking For

  • 5–6+ years' experience in Operations or a similar generalist role, including experience leading on one of the key areas (people operations, legal, compliance or IT).

  • Experience in high-growth startups is a must.

  • A whizz AI, tooling and automation.

  • Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

Compensation and Benefits

At Magentic, we recognise and reward the talent that drives our success. We offer:

  • Competitive Equity: play a real part in Magentic’s upside.

  • Salary: £100,000 - £110,000 per annum

  • Private healthcare

  • Hybrid London HQ (4 days in the office).

  • Company provided meals at the office

  • Monthly “Social budget” to spend getting to know your colleagues (coffee, food, activities, etc.)

  • Work from anywhere 4 weeks out of the year

  • Salary sacrifice pension and nursery schemes

  • Annual team retreat—a fully-funded off-site to recharge, bond, and build.

Our Interview Process

We can move quickly through these stages, so let us know if you have any timelines we need to meet.

  1. Initial call (30 mins): this first step is an opportunity for you to hear more about Magentic and the role, and for us to learn more about how your experience aligns with the role.

  2. Skills interview (45 mins): in this step, we'll ask you to prepare a presentation and take Q&A.

  3. In-person interview (half-day, paid): for the final step, we invite you to come meet the team in-person. We find this is the best way for candidates to get a sense of what working at Magentic is like. This day will include a culture interview, founder interview and a presentation task / discussion with the team.

Equal Opportunities and Accommodations Statement

At Magentic, our mission is to build AI that helps solve some of the world's most complex real world problems. We believe building a diverse workforce will be the key to solving this for our customers.

 

Magentic is committed to creating a truly inclusive team and we’re proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. As we grow, we're intentional about building teams with a broad range of backgrounds, experiences and viewpoints, recognising that this leads to better ideas, stronger collaboration and better outcomes for our customers therefore we strongly encourage applications from all backgrounds and cultures to apply.

 

We recognise that some groups remain underrepresented within the industry and are committed to creating an environment that celebrates and supports everyone.

 

Everyone works differently, and we want to ensure our interview process gives you the best chance to show us what you can do. If you require any reasonable adjustments or accommodations, please let us know and we'll work with you to make the process accessible.

 

Responsible AI Statement

At Magentic, we are committed to developing artificial intelligence that benefits humanity. We push the limits of AI's capabilities and are dedicated to its responsible and safe deployment. Recognising the profound impact of AI, we ensure that its development is centred around human needs and safety, incorporating a wide array of perspectives to fulfil our mission.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager
jobs.description:
Swarm Aero is redefining air power, building the largest swarming UAV and the most versatile swarming aircraft network in the world. The company is moving quickly to launch the first aircraft designed specifically for swarming, as well as the Command & Control software to mobilize swarms of thousands of heterogeneous autonomous assets and empower human operators to achieve superhuman results.

The team has created and exited multiple startups, negotiated defense deals worth billions of dollars, and designed and built 30+ novel aircraft, with aerospace experience from Scaled Composites, Airbus, Archer Aviation, Blue Origin, and Boom Supersonic.

Mission

Turn operational needs, customer feedback, and product direction into clear product specifications—and then drive those capabilities through decisions, design, development, and validation.

You will work directly with the Head of Product on Legion and become a core contributor to both defining the product and running the process around it.

What You’ll Own

  • Create clear, detailed product specifications for new features and capabilities.

  • Take customer needs, operator feedback, technical constraints, and product direction and turn them into actionable product requirements.

  • Own bounded features from early definition through design, development, feedback, and validation.

  • Work directly with Product Design to translate specifications into detailed workflows and Figma designs.

  • Review designs and implementations against product intent and requirements.

  • Facilitate product discussions with government customers, third-party contractors, operators, engineers, and internal stakeholders.

  • Prepare agendas and clearly identify topics requiring feedback, decisions, or alignment.

  • Capture decisions, unresolved issues, customer feedback, and action items.

  • Incorporate meeting outcomes directly into product specifications and related artifacts.

  • Maintain feature status, decision history, feedback registers, and key product commitments.

  • Identify ambiguity, conflicting requirements, and missing decisions before they slow the team down.

  • Track important product and contractual deliverables.

  • Help prepare product reviews, demonstrations, and customer discussions.

  • Create enough structure to keep the organization aligned without introducing unnecessary process.

What Great Looks Like

You are given a problem such as:

“Operators need a better way to understand and respond to vehicle health issues during degraded communications.”

You meet with the relevant operators, engineers, customers, and stakeholders.

You understand the underlying problem.

You separate customer requests from actual product requirements.

You identify edge cases and unresolved decisions.

You write a product specification that clearly explains the intended behavior, workflows, system states, requirements, and open questions.

You work with Product Design to turn that specification into a strong interface.

You incorporate feedback, resolve ambiguity, and keep the feature moving until the capability works as intended.

The Head of Product provides direction and reviews the most important decisions—but does not need to personally produce every artifact or manage every follow-up.

Early Expectations

Within the first few weeks, you should begin contributing directly to product specifications.

Initially, you may draft sections of specifications or own smaller, well-bounded capabilities with guidance from the Head of Product.

As your understanding of Legion, its operators, and the technical architecture grows, you will rapidly take ownership of larger features.

We are not looking for someone who spends six months observing before contributing.

The Person We’re Looking For

You are an excellent writer.

You can take a complicated conversation and turn it into a clear product definition.

You have strong product judgment and are comfortable making reasonable decisions when requirements are incomplete.

You understand that a customer request is not automatically a product requirement.

You are technically curious and capable of participating meaningfully in discussions with software engineers, systems engineers, operators, and external partners.

You naturally ask questions like:

  • What problem are we actually trying to solve?

  • Who needs this capability?

  • What should happen in this edge case?

  • What does the operator see?

  • What state is the system actually in?

  • How will we know this works?

  • Is this a product decision, an engineering decision, or a customer preference?

  • You are highly organized, but organization is a means to an end.

  • Your real job is creating clarity and moving product decisions forward.

Particularly Valuable Experience

Experience with any of the following would be especially valuable:

  • Technical product management

  • Complex B2B software

  • Command-and-control systems

  • Aerospace or defense

  • Robotics or autonomous systems

  • Mission planning

  • Geospatial software

  • Systems engineering

  • Government programs

  • Operational testing

  • Requirements development

What This Role Is Not

This is not a project coordinator role.

It is not a Scrum Master role.

It is not an administrative Product Operations position.

It is not someone whose primary contribution is scheduling meetings, maintaining Jira, or writing meeting minutes.

Those activities may occasionally be necessary, but they are secondary.

The primary contribution is:

understanding product problems and defining excellent solutions.

Success After 90 Days

  • You are independently drafting product specifications for bounded Legion features.

  • Customer and operator feedback is consistently translated into clear product requirements.

  • Product meetings result in updated specifications, decisions, and actionable follow-up.

  • The Head of Product can delegate meaningful feature-definition work to you.

  • Product Design receives clearer inputs and can move faster.

  • Important product decisions and rationale are documented and traceable.

ITAR requirement

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

Swarm Aero is an equal opportunity employer. We value diverse backgrounds and experiences and make employment decisions without regard to race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, or disability.

What We Offer

  • Meaningful equity in a high-growth defense technology company

  • Competitive base salary commensurate with experience

  • Medical, dental, vision, and 401k

  • PTO and paid sick leave

  • Monthly wellness stipend

  • Daily catered lunch (office)

  • Paid parental leave

  • Direct impact on a critical national security mission

  • A world-class team of engineers and operators solving genuinely hard problems

jobs.title: Golang Backend Engineer, Financial Product Fraud
jobs.description:
Our Global Structure


Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team.

Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person.

We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform.

This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch.

We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one.

This role will be based in London, UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin.

What you'll do:

  • Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers.
  • Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout.
  • Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times.
  • Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer.
  • Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter.
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team.
  • Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event.

Our expectations:

  • 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production.
  • 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly.
  • A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar).
  • Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability.
  • Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality.

Nice to have

  • Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud.
  • Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path.
  • Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go.
  • Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).
  • Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes.

What we value

  • A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output.
  • Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them.
  • A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments.
  • Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together.
  • An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.

We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
About Payflows

At Payflows, we build software that helps large companies manage and automate their payment workflows. It’s not the flashiest part of a business, but it’s one of the most critical: invoices, approvals, payments, and controls. When these things slow down, the whole company feels it.

But our ambition goes further than just building a better workflow tool.

We believe the future of finance operations is not faster clicking: it’s no clicking at all 🫳 🎤

Finance teams shouldn’t spend their days moving data from one screen to another. Software should do the operational work, and humans should focus on reviewing, approving, and making the decisions that matter.

That’s the direction we’re building toward: an agent-driven finance platform, where intelligent agents handle the repetitive tasks, and users stay in control.

We started in 2022 with a small team and a rough first version of the product. Three years later, we’re working with major companies across France, the UK, and the US while choosing to keep our team small and human-sized.

We moved fast, shipped a lot, and not everything was built in a perfect way. But it helped us learn quickly, sign real customers, and prove that the problem we’re solving truly matters.

In 2024, investors trusted us with a $25M Series A. That gives us the chance to keep growing while also strengthening our foundations and building the system that will power this agent-driven future.

Today, we’re about 35 people from many different countries, and we’re looking for a few amazing humans to join the next chapter. 🤗

🚀 What you’ll actually do

You’ll help build a product that real finance teams rely on every day.

For us, engineering is not just about clean code, it’s about reliability, clarity, and trust, especially when money and automation are involved.

In a typical week, you might:

  • Design and implement new services for a product feature.

  • Refactor an early service to make it more robust.

  • Investigate a performance or production issue.

  • Work with product and frontend to shape a new feature.

  • Review code and help teammates improve.

  • Build backend tools that our AI agents use to perform real finance operations.

  • Design safe, deterministic workflows where agents propose actions and humans review them.

Your time will be split between building new features and improving what already exists. Both matter.

You won’t just build endpoints. You’ll help shape the execution layer that our agents rely on: the APIs, data models, and workflows that let them act safely in production.

You’ll work closely with product, frontend, and customer-facing teams. We expect engineers to take ownership of parts of the system and help make them more reliable over time.

💻 Our current tech reality

Our stack evolves based on our challenges, but we care more about good design than trendy tools 🙏

Python is our core language. It helps us move fast, keep the code readable, and fits naturally with our AI-driven approach. A growing part of the system is built around agents that use our backend as a set of reliable, deterministic tools.

  • Core language: Python

  • Backend: FastAPI + Pydantic

  • Data: PostgreSQL

  • Infra: AWS, serverless when it makes sense

  • Performance: some Rust for critical paths

  • Architecture: multi-service backend, simple enough to reason about

Some parts of the system are clean and well-tested. Others were built quickly and need love. That’s the phase we’re in.

Over the next year, we’ll focus on:

  • Turning core workflows into reliable tools for our agents

  • Simplifying services

  • Improving tests and observability

  • Making performance more predictable

  • Cleaning up early code

We know we’re not perfect, but we care a lot about improving step by step.


✨ Who’s going to thrive with us

You’ll probably feel comfortable here if:

  • You like building products people actually use.

  • You are autonomous and take ownership of what you ship.

  • You take initiative and lead by example.

  • You’re curious and enjoy figuring things out.

  • You’re pragmatic about trade-offs.

  • You communicate with kindness and clarity.

This role is a great fit if you’re excited by the idea of:

  • Building systems that are used by AI agents, not just humans.

  • Designing reliable, safe automation in production.

  • Working on a product that is still early and evolving quickly.

You don’t need to know everything about AI. But you should be curious about it and excited to work in a system where agents are part of the core product 🤖

🧩 What you’ll get from this role

  • Real ownership over parts of the system.

  • Direct impact on customers and product decisions.

  • A small, human team where your work is visible and meaningful 🤝

  • A mix of feature work, system design, and technical improvements.

  • Exposure to real scaling and production challenges.

We offer:

  • A high-autonomy environment where you have real ownership and space to make an impact.

  • A culture based on trust, ownership, and clear communication.

jobs.title: DevOps / Infra Lead
jobs.description:
🌍 Our Vision & Mission

At Payflows, we give finance teams the tools to reclaim their time and energy. Our platform weaves together banking connectivity, payments, AI, and procurement so they can ditch the busywork and focus on what really moves the needle.

🤝 Why Join Us?

We’re a small, mighty team who’ve earned our stripes at Airbnb, Luko, BNP Paribas, and Facebook. It’s not always easy—things move fast, and we expect a lot—but if you’re hungry for impact, you’ll find it here.

🛠️ We’re builders at heart. We move fast, think deeply, ship often — and we’re always hungry to learn more. You'll collaborate closely with product and tech to craft elegant backend systems that scale as fast as we do.

🚀 What You’ll Do

You'll own the infrastructure for a product that real finance teams rely on every day.

For us, infrastructure is not just about uptime; it's about reliability, security, and trust - especially when money and automation are involved. The platform has to be boring in the best possible way: predictable, observable, and safe to deploy to.

  • In a typical week, you might:

    • Evolve our infrastructure-as-code to add a service, a queue, or a whole new environment.

    • Improve our CI/CD pipelines so engineers ship safely and fast, dozens of times a day.

    • Investigate a production issue: a latency spike, a failing deploy, a database under load.

    • Strengthen observability with dashboards, alerts, and traces, so we catch problems before customers do.

    • Harden our security, secrets management, and access controls.

    • Tune cost and performance across our AWS footprint.

Your time will be split between building new platform capabilities and making what already exists more reliable. Both matter.

You'll help shape the foundation that everything else stands on: the pipelines, environments, and guardrails that let engineers and our AI agents act safely in production.

You'll work closely with backend, frontend, and the AI team. We expect you to take ownership of the platform and make it more reliable over time, not wait for tickets.

💻 Our current tech reality

Our stack evolves based on our challenges, but we care more about good design than trendy tools

We're an AWS shop, and we lean on managed services and infrastructure-as-code so the system is reproducible and easy to reason with. A growing part of our world is making the backend a set of reliable, deterministic tools that AI agents can call, which raises the bar on reliability even further.

  • Cloud: AWS

  • Infra-as-code: Pulumi (Python)

  • Compute: ECS + Lambda, serverless when it makes sense

  • Data: PostgreSQL on RDS/Aurora

  • CI/CD: GitLab CI

  • Orchestration: Airflow (MWAA)

  • Observability: Grafana Cloud, CloudWatch, Sentry

  • Auth & identity: Cognito, IAM

  • Edge & frontend: API Gateway, ALB, AWS Amplify for the web app

Some of this is clean, version-controlled, and reproducible. Other parts grew fast and live a little too much in people’s heads instead of in code. Closing that gap is a big part of why this role exists.

Over the next year, we'll focus on:

  • Making every environment reproducible from code

  • Better observability and alerting, fewer surprises

  • Tightening the security and compliance posture that comes with handling enterprise finance data

  • Faster, safer deploys

  • Keeping AWS costs sane as we scale


🧑‍💻 What we’re looking for

  • 5+ years of experience with Python or any other OOP language

  • Backend expertise: APIs, microservices, architecture best practices

  • Databases & SQL: Data modeling, query optimization

  • Git lover: Comfortable with version control and code reviews

  • Pragmatic engineering mindset: Build, test, refine, simplify—smart shortcuts when time is tight

🧩 Bonus points if you’ve worked on:

  • B2B SaaS or finance/ERP tools

  • BaaS APIs or payment infra

  • Serverless, AWS, event-driven architecture exposure

✨ Who's going to thrive with us

You'll probably feel comfortable here if:

  • You think in systems and instinctively automate yourself out of repetitive work.

  • You treat infrastructure as code, not as pets.

  • You stay calm during incidents and are genuinely good at root-causing.

  • You care about security, because you're handling other people's money.

  • You are autonomous and take ownership of what you ship.

  • You take initiative and lead by example.

  • You're pragmatic about trade-offs.

  • You communicate with kindness and clarity.

You don't need to know everything about AI - but you must be curious about it and excited to build the reliable foundation that agents run on 🤖

🧩 What you'll get from this role

  • Real ownership over the platform the whole company runs on.

  • Direct impact on reliability, security, and how fast every engineer can ship.

  • A mix of platform building, system design, and reliability work.

  • Exposure to real scaling and production challenges.

  • Je beschikt over bewezen probleemoplossende vaardigheden en een proactieve gedrevenheid om te leren hoe nieuwe technologieën werken.

  • Je bent sociaal vaardig, spreekt vloeiend professioneel Engels en hebt een oprechte klantgerichte mindset.

  • Je beheerst de Nederlandse taal.

  • Je bent minimaal 3 dagen per week aanwezig op kantoor.

Senior Software-Entwickler (m/w/d) – PHP/Symfony & React – Berlin

Der Plan steht, jetzt fehlst du: Bring unsere Software von Legacy-PHP auf Symfony und React.

Auf einen Blick

  • Stack: PHP 8.1 (Legacy) → Symfony · jQuery/Vanilla-JS → React · MySQL/MariaDB, SingleStore · Git, CI/CD

  • Vertrag: unbefristet, Vollzeit

  • Arbeitsmodell: hybrid, 3 Tage Büro / 2 Tage remote

  • Standort: Berlin-Zehlendorf, direkt am S-Bahnhof Zehlendorf (S1)

  • Produkt: Konsentas, ein Termin- und Vorgangsmanagement für Behörden

  • Start: so bald wie möglich oder nach Vereinbarung

Die Rolle

Unser Kernprodukt Konsentas ist über viele Jahre gewachsen, und das sieht man dem Code an. Das Backend läuft auf PHP 8.1 ohne Framework. Im Frontend stehen jQuery und Vanilla-JS neben React, und automatisierte Tests gibt es bisher wenige.

Wohin es gehen soll, ist klar: Das Backend wird schrittweise auf Symfony umgestellt, das Frontend auf React vereinheitlicht. Bis Ende 2027 soll die Migration abgeschlossen sein. Was dafür fehlt, ist kein Plan, sondern Kapazität.

Du triffst eigenständig technische Entscheidungen, bringst dich in Architektur- und Modernisierungsfragen ein und sorgst dafür, dass die Codequalität mit jedem Release besser wird. Dabei bleibt das Produkt im Einsatz: Wartung, Support und neue Features laufen parallel zur Modernisierung.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Legacy-Module bei laufendem Betrieb schrittweise durch Symfony-Services und React-Oberflächen ersetzen

  • Fullstack-Features von der Datenbank bis zum Frontend entwickeln, teils auch als kundenspezifische Erweiterungen

  • Bestehenden Legacy-Code pflegen, debuggen und weiterentwickeln

  • Code-Reviews durchführen und die Testabdeckung ausbauen

  • Mit Entwicklungsleitung und Geschäftsführung abstimmen, welche Bereiche als Nächstes modernisiert werden

  • Unsere zwei Auszubildenden im letzten Ausbildungsabschnitt fachlich begleiten (ohne disziplinarische Führung)

  • Gelegentlich an Kundenterminen teilnehmen, etwa alle 3–4 Wochen

Nach 6 Monaten …

… setzt du Features eigenständig um, hast spürbar zur Modernisierung beigetragen, die Codequalität verbessert und bist für unsere Azubis eine feste Ansprechperson.

Dein Profil

  • Erfahrung: etwa 4–5 Jahre in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung (ein Richtwert, keine harte Grenze)

  • PHP: fundierte Kenntnisse in modernem PHP 8.x mit objektorientierter Architektur, etwa Dependency Injection, Interfaces und SOLID

  • Symfony: nachweisbare Praxiserfahrung mit dem Framework

  • Legacy-Code: Du gehst sicher mit gewachsenen Codebasen um. Du refaktorierst, debuggst und entwickelst weiter, ohne alles neu zu schreiben.

  • JavaScript/React: solide Erfahrung im Frontend, jQuery schreckt dich nicht ab

  • Datenbanken: relationale Datenbanken wie MySQL/MariaDB oder SingleStore und sicherer Umgang mit SQL

  • Tooling: Git und Arbeit mit CI/CD

  • Sprache: Deutsch auf C1-Niveau, Englisch mindestens B1

  • Arbeitsweise: eigenständig, strukturiert, proaktiv und mit hohem Qualitätsanspruch

  • Persönlich: Du kommunizierst verlässlich, arbeitest gern im Team, übernimmst Verantwortung, hast keine Angst vor schwierigen Codestellen und gibst dein Wissen gern weiter.

  • Abschluss: Ausbildung oder FH-Abschluss zählen bei uns genauso viel wie ein Uni-Studium. Entscheidend ist deine Praxiserfahrung.

Pluspunkte: REST/API-Design und Schnittstellenentwicklung, automatisiertes Testing (PHPUnit, Jest), Docker, Deployment-Pipelines und Cloud, Software-Architektur und Design

-

Patterns, produktiver Einsatz von KI-Tools wie Claude Code oder Codex. Erfahrung mit Software für den öffentlichen Sektor ist nicht nötig.

Dein Team

Ein kleines Team mit kurzen Wegen: Daniel (Developer Lead), Nico (Geschäftsführer & Projektmanager), der selbst aktiv mitentwickelt, ein externer Entwickler und zwei Auszubildende. Ihr stimmt euch täglich ab. Daniel und Nico übernehmen dein Onboarding persönlich.

Was wir bieten

  • Ein sinnstiftendes Produkt, das täglich in Bürgerämtern genutzt wird, in einem krisensicheren Markt

  • Echter Einfluss auf technische Entscheidungen und eine Modernisierung mit klarem Ziel

  • 30 Urlaubstage

  • Gleitzeit mit Kernzeit ab 10 Uhr, 2 Remote-Tage pro Woche

  • Weiterbildung während der Arbeitszeit, z. B. Udemy-Kurse; eigene Vorschläge sind willkommen

  • Claude-Lizenz, offen für weitere Tools

  • Hardware: Lenovo ThinkPad, offen für Vorschläge

  • UrbanSportsClub und JobRad

  • Gute Anbindung: S1 und Busse M48, 101, 115

So läuft der Bewerbungsprozess

  1. Kennenlerngespräch mit Sara

  2. Technisches Interview mit Live-Projektarbeit mit Nico und Daniel

  3. Teamgespräch vor Ort

  4. Angebot

Über Girona

Seit über 25 Jahren entwickelt die Girona Softwareentwicklung GmbH in Berlin Software für die öffentliche Verwaltung. Städte wie Berlin, München, Bonn und Dessau setzen seit Jahrzehnten auf unsere Lösungen, Konsentas etwa in Bürgerämtern, Gesundheitsämtern sowie Kfz-Zulassungs- und Führerscheinstellen.

Du willst ein bewährtes Produkt fit für die Zukunft machen? Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung.

jobs.title: Data Privacy Analyst - Regulatory Compliance
jobs.description:
The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The Compliance team’s mission is to keep iwoca a safe and trusted lender for UK small businesses, and to make the compliant path the easy path for the teams we work with.

We make sure iwoca meets its regulatory obligations, particularly the financial crime, sanctions and data protection requirements that apply across our suite of products and services.

We are the second line of defence for the UK business. We advise the people building and running the business on what the rules require, set the policies and standards they work to, and test whether what happens in practice matches them. We work alongside the product teams so that each product meets its obligations and can grow.

Data protection is central to what we do. We hold the data privacy function for the UK business and own how iwoca handles personal data end to end: the lawful basis for how customer, applicant and third-party data is used; data subject access requests and other individual rights; personal data breaches; retention and deletion; records of processing; marketing and consent; the privacy review of new products and features; and the governance of automated decisioning and AI tooling.


How we work:

  • We enable rather than block. The answer is rarely just “no” — it’s what it would take to get to yes, and what the firm is accepting if it goes ahead anyway.

  • We go to the source. Positions are grounded in the actual rule, regulation or guidance, and we can show where they come from.

  • We’re proportionate. Controls match the risk in front of us. We don’t build process for its own sake.

  • We’re close to the business. We work directly with Tech, Data, Credit, Operations and Legal, and we want to be in the room early rather than at the end.

The role

As Data Privacy Analyst you will run iwoca’s day-to-day UK data protection work and help the business apply UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR in practice. Your primary focus will be the statutory core: data subject access requests, data protection impact assessments, legitimate interests assessments, personal data breaches and records of processing.

The role is not only to run that work but to improve it. A significant part of the job is identifying where our privacy operations could be automated, supported by AI or otherwise improved, assessing what each option would take and what it would mean for compliance, and specifying it well enough for our Tech and Data teams to deliver.

There is real room for the role to grow: as you build credibility, so does the scope, towards owning areas of the framework outright, leading on AI and automation governance, and taking a larger advisory remit across the business.

You will report to the Data Privacy Manager and work closely with the Head of Compliance who also acts as iwoca’s DPO, so you will have experienced support on the harder judgement calls. This is a hands-on role and the work is visible — much of it goes to senior stakeholders or to the regulator.

Impact and influence

  • Individual rights and data breaches. Own data subject access requests from intake to response — scoping the search, applying exemptions and meeting the statutory deadline — along with erasure, rectification and objection requests. Triage and investigate suspected personal data breaches, assess them against the 72-hour notification test, and keep the breach register accurate.

  • Privacy assessments and advice. Assist with DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments and other privacy reviews on new products, features, suppliers and data flows. Be an accessible first point of contact for teams across iwoca with a data protection question, and give them an answer they can act on, early enough to shape what they build.

  • Records, policies and reporting. Keep the record of processing activities accurate as the business changes, hold the retention and deletion schedules to account, review data processing agreements with suppliers, help maintain our data protection policies and standards, and produce the privacy reporting that goes to senior stakeholders.

  • AI and automated decisioning. Help assess AI tooling and automated decision-making across lending and operations: what personal data goes in, what lawful basis supports it, what the model does with it, and what rights customers have over the outcome. That includes the risks specific to these systems — decisions taken without meaningful human involvement, bias in outcomes, unreliable model output — and recommending how we address them.

  • Automation and improvement. Identify the manual steps in our privacy operations that should not be manual, assess the options, and set out the requirements and compliance implications clearly enough for Tech and Data to deliver them.

The requirements

Essential skills

  • Experience. Experience in data protection or privacy operations, or in a compliance, legal, risk or operational role where data protection was a real part of the job.

  • Data protection knowledge. A solid practical understanding of UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and PECR, and of how the ICO expects firms to apply them. Familiarity with the changes made by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 is an advantage.

  • Privacy operations and assessments. Hands-on experience of statutory work: DSARs, DPIAs, legitimate interests assessments, breach handling, ROPA maintenance or data processing agreement review. You may not have done all of these — but we want to see that you have done some of them properly.

  • AI and automation. A real interest in, and working understanding of, how data protection law applies to AI and automated decision-making. Enough technical fluency to see where a manual process could be automated, set out what is needed, and hold your own in a conversation with engineers.

  • Stakeholder management: Comfortable dealing directly with product, engineering, marketing, credit and operations teams, and able to give a non-specialist a clear answer they can act on rather than a legal summary.

Bonus:

  • Sector experience. Financial services or fintech, ideally in lending or payments.

  • Credentials. A privacy or AI qualification such as CIPP/E, CIPM, or ICO-recognised practitioner certificates — or working towards one.

  • Practical tooling. Experience using Claude Code, LLMs or privacy management platforms.

The culture

At iwoca, we prioritise a culture of learning, growth, and support, and invest in the development of our team members. We value thought and skill diversity, and encourage people to explore new areas of interest, adopt better tools – including AI – and apply sound judgement so our products and decisions improve over time.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A choice between a dedicated dental plan or a health cash plan that reimburses everyday medical expenses.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

jobs.description:
Über Helix

Bei Helix entwickeln wir einen live KI-Coach, der Vertrieblern während den deals hilft diese zu gewinnen. mehr auf helix-cx.com

Wir sind ein junges Startup aus München und suchen ambitionierte Studierende, die gemeinsam mit uns wachsen, vom ersten Tag an Verantwortung übernehmen und einen der wertvollsten Skills im Geschäftsleben entwickeln wollen: Vertrieb.

Über die Rolle

Als Business Development Representative (BDR) hilfst du uns dabei, unseren Outbound-Vertrieb aufzubauen und neue Geschäftsmöglichkeiten zu schaffen.

Du bist der erste Kontaktpunkt für potenzielle Kunden, identifizierst ihre Herausforderungen, weckst Interesse an unserer Lösung und verwandelst erste Gespräche in qualifizierte Verkaufschancen.

Das ist eine praktische Vertriebsrolle. Einen großen Teil deiner Zeit wirst du mit Cold Calling verbringen, direkt mit Entscheidern sprechen, Einwände behandeln und lernen, wie man neue Kunden gewinnt.

Du arbeitest eng mit den Gründern zusammen, erhältst direktes Feedback und übernimmst von Anfang an echte Verantwortung.

Deine Perspektive: Diese Rolle soll mehr sein als ein klassischer Werkstudentenjob. Bei guter Performance hast du die Möglichkeit, dich zum Account Executive (AE) weiterzuentwickeln, eigene Verkaufschancen zu übernehmen und schließlich selbstständig Deals abzuschließen.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Prospecting: Identifiziere und recherchiere potenzielle Kunden, Zielunternehmen und relevante Entscheidungsträger.

  • Outbound Sales: Übernimm die aktive Ansprache potenzieller Kunden durch Cold Calling, E-Mail und LinkedIn, um qualifizierte Verkaufschancen zu generieren.

  • Kundengespräche: Verstehe die Herausforderungen potenzieller Kunden, vermittle den Mehrwert unserer Lösung, behandle Einwände und vereinbare Termine.

  • Sales Strategy: Teste unterschiedliche Ansprachemethoden, Botschaften und Vertriebstechniken, um unsere Conversion Rates kontinuierlich zu verbessern.

  • Pipeline Development: Hilf dabei, unsere Sales-Pipeline aufzubauen und zu verwalten und erste Gespräche in konkrete Geschäftsmöglichkeiten zu verwandeln.

  • Deal Ownership: Übernimm mit wachsender Erfahrung mehr Verantwortung im gesamten Sales-Prozess – von Discovery Calls bis hin zum eigenständigen Abschluss von Deals.

Was wir dir bieten

  • Schnelle Karriereentwicklung: Die Möglichkeit, dich vom BDR zum Account Executive weiterzuentwickeln, eigene Deals zu übernehmen und deine Karriere im B2B-Vertrieb aufzubauen.

  • Ungedeckelte Provision: Leistung zählt. Je erfolgreicher du bist, desto mehr kannst du verdienen – ohne Obergrenze bei der Provision.

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Gründern: Arbeite eng mit dem Gründerteam zusammen, erhalte persönliches Coaching und lerne, wie man ein Unternehmen von Grund auf aufbaut.

  • Echte Verantwortung: Du bist nicht hier, um nur zuzuschauen. Du übernimmst eigenständig die Kundenansprache, sprichst mit echten Entscheidern und trägst direkt zu unserem Wachstum bei.

  • Flexible Teilzeit: Verbinde dein Studium mit einer verantwortungsvollen Tätigkeit in einem schnell wachsenden Startup.

  • KI- und Startup-Erfahrung: Arbeite an der Schnittstelle von künstlicher Intelligenz, Technologie und Business Development.

Was wir von dir erwarten

  • Du bist aktuell an einer Universität oder Hochschule eingeschrieben und möchtest neben deinem Studium praktische Business-Erfahrung sammeln.

  • Du verfügst über ausgezeichnete Deutschkenntnisse und hast Spaß daran, mit Menschen zu kommunizieren.

  • Du bist ehrgeizig, proaktiv und motiviert, messbare Ergebnisse zu erzielen.

  • Du hast kein Problem damit, auf fremde Menschen zuzugehen, Fragen zu stellen und mit Ablehnung umzugehen.

  • Du interessierst dich für KI, Startups und die Frage, wie Unternehmen wachsen.

  • Du arbeitest zuverlässig, eigenständig und möchtest dich kontinuierlich verbessern.

  • Erste Erfahrungen in Sales, Business Development, Recruiting, Consulting oder anderen kundenorientierten Tätigkeiten sind ein Plus, aber keine Voraussetzung.

Dein Ehrgeiz, deine Einstellung und deine Lernbereitschaft sind uns wichtiger als deine bisherige Erfahrung oder deine Noten.

Warum Helix?

Lerne einen der wertvollsten Skills im Geschäftsleben.
Egal, ob du später selbst gründen, ins Consulting gehen oder eine Karriere im Vertrieb aufbauen möchtest: Die Fähigkeit, überzeugend zu kommunizieren, zu verhandeln und zu verkaufen, wird dir immer einen entscheidenden Vorteil verschaffen.

Bei Helix lernst du durch praktische Erfahrung. Du sprichst mit echten Entscheidern, verstehst, wie Unternehmen Kaufentscheidungen treffen, und erlebst aus erster Hand, wie aus einem ersten Gespräch ein zahlender Kunde wird.

Wachse mit dem Unternehmen.
Wir bauen unseren Vertrieb von Grund auf auf. Das bedeutet, dass du die Möglichkeit hast, Prozesse mitzugestalten, neue Strategien zu testen und Verantwortung zu übernehmen, für die du in einem größeren Unternehmen normalerweise deutlich länger brauchen würdest.

Deine Leistung bestimmt deine Möglichkeiten.
Wir suchen Menschen, die lernen und Verantwortung übernehmen wollen. Wenn du konstant gute Ergebnisse lieferst, bekommst du die Möglichkeit, über die reine Kundenakquise hinauszuwachsen, eigene Verkaufsgespräche zu führen und Deals abzuschließen.

Wisse, worauf du dich einlässt.
Vertrieb ist nicht immer einfach. Du wirst viele Anrufe tätigen, häufig ein Nein hören und Gespräche führen, die zu nichts führen. Gleichzeitig entwickelst du dadurch Durchhaltevermögen, Selbstbewusstsein und die Fähigkeit, andere Menschen zu überzeugen – Fähigkeiten, die dich dein gesamtes Berufsleben begleiten werden.

So bewirbst du dich

Wir suchen keinen perfekten Lebenslauf und erwarten keine jahrelange Berufserfahrung.

Stell dich noch in einem video kurz vor, erzähle uns, was du studierst und warum du Lust auf Vertrieb hast.

Wir möchten vor allem einen ersten Eindruck von dir als Person bekommen. Ein professionell produziertes Video ist nicht notwendig.

Wenn du ehrgeizig bist, Herausforderungen magst und lernen möchtest, wie man erfolgreich verkauft, freuen wir uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen.

Every 10 minutes, 18 million conversations happen between businesses and consumers around the world.

For decades, the consumer side of those conversations sucked: long queues, robotic menus, repeated explanations, and advice that is often unhelpful. Most people today still cannot simply say what their problem is in natural language when communicating with businesses.

AI changes that. For the first time, companies can have natural conversations with customers at massive scale. Every B2C company - from energy providers to telcos to insurers - will use AI agents to talk to their customers. The number of conversations businesses will handle is going to explode in the coming years.

At telli, we are solving the challenges that come with that shift. Today, leading B2C companies like Sky are already using telli to deploy thousands of voice agents to provide their customers with a new experience. But building a first voice agent is easy, getting it to drive real outcomes for customers and businesses is the hard part. telli helps companies build, deploy, and improve consumer-facing AI voice agents at scale. This will become one of the most important software categories of the next decade, and we intend to win it.

We are a small, AI-pilled team that likes to solve hard problems. Be it engineering, product, or GTM - we build, experiment, and move fast, while heavily leveraging the capabilities of AI models. jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist
jobs.description:
OUR MISSION

To become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.

What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.

In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.

And we’re a long way from done!

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join our award-winning Data Science team at a pivotal moment. Carwow operates a two-sided marketplace — connecting car buyers and sellers at scale — and data science sits at the heart of how we make that marketplace smarter, faster, and more valuable for everyone in it. In fact, we recently won GenAI initiative of the Year at the British Data Awards.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role working centrally across the business. You'll partner with teams spanning Commercial, Marketing, Product, Finance, Engineering and Operations — developing and deploying ML and AI solutions that drive outcomes across both sides of our marketplace. The problems you'll work on are genuinely varied: pricing models, propensity and demand signals that sharpen marketing spend, personalised recommendations for our web product and CRM, and LLM-powered solutions for operational challenges like document verification.

You'll translate ambiguous business problems into structured, production-ready solutions — and you'll be expected to deliver them end-to-end, from first principles through to being deployment-ready and beyond.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

  • End-to-End ML & AI Delivery: Lead data science initiatives from problem framing through to deployment, monitoring, and iteration — delivering the full production lifecycle. With no dedicated ML engineering function, you'll be responsible for ensuring your solutions are robust, scalable, and performing in the real world long after they ship.

  • GenAI & LLM Application: Design and build LLM-powered solutions where they create genuine business value — document processing, intelligent search, content understanding, and beyond. Apply them alongside classical ML with clear judgement about where each approach earns its place.

  • Commercial Impact: Connect your work directly to business outcomes. Whether you're building a model to improve marketing efficiency, a pricing signal to sharpen commercial decisions, or a recommendation engine to increase conversion — you understand the business lever you're pulling and design your solutions accordingly.

  • Prototyping & Experimentation: Move fast to test ideas before committing to full-scale development. Define rigorous success metrics upfront, validate honestly, and know when to double down and when to walk away.

  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Work closely with Commercial, Marketing, Product, Finance, Engineering and Operations stakeholders to understand problems deeply before reaching for a solution. Translate findings into clear, actionable narratives for both technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Standards & Craft: Contribute to shared best practices, documentation, and ways of working that raise the bar for the data science function — and help more junior team members grow alongside you. Drive continued adoption of AI capabilities to drive efficiencies, automation and constantly leverage new capabilities.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

Please note: We know that no candidate will be the perfect match for all we've listed in this posting, so we’d encourage you to apply if you feel you're close to the brief but not an exact match. Ideally you’ll have

  • Commercial Mindset: You think about business impact first. You understand how your models connect to revenue, efficiency, or customer outcomes — and you use that to prioritise, scope, and communicate your work.

  • Stakeholder Partnership: Proven ability to work with commercial, marketing, and product stakeholders — translating business problems into well-scoped solutions and communicating technical solutions, challenges and outcomes clearly at all levels.

  • Sound Judgement: You navigate the tooling landscape with clear eyes — knowing when classical ML is right, when GenAI unlocks something new, and when a simpler solution is the more honest answer. Strong instincts for scalability, reliability, and explainability.

  • [Bonus] Marketplace or Two-Sided Platform Experience: Understanding of supply/demand dynamics and how data science creates leverage in a marketplace context.

TEHCNICAL SKILLSET

  • Proven ML Experience: A strong track record of building, deploying, and maintaining ML models in Python in a production environment — not just notebooks. You've owned models after they ship and know how to keep them healthy.

  • Full-Lifecycle Delivery (MLOps): Comfortable delivering the end-to-end production lifecycle — model training, versioning, monitoring, and champion/challenger experimentation — without relying on a dedicated ML engineering team to carry that responsibility.

  • GenAI & LLM Expertise: Hands-on experience building LLM-powered solutions that deliver measurable business value. You understand how to apply, evaluate, and extend these tools — and you're honest about where they fall short.

  • Technical Depth: Solid experience in a cloud ML environment with software engineering principles — version control, code reviews, unit testing, and familiarity with containerisation.

  • Quantitative Rigour: Strong foundation in statistical evaluation and experiment design. You can define and defend success metrics, and you know when a model is degrading and what to do about it.

  • [Bonus] Experience with VertexAI

TOOLS & TECHNOLOGIES

  • Languages: Python, SQL

  • Data & Transformation: dbt, Snowflake, BigQuery

  • Visualisation & BI: Looker

  • Engineering & MLOps: Docker, GitHub

  • Workflow & Orchestration: Vertex AI Pipelines (GCP), Kubeflow

  • LLMs & GenAI: Gemini API, Claude API

jobs.description:
Head of Product - Cards

Build with us

Businesses deserve better from finance. Less friction, more freedom. Since 2004, Mollie has been on a mission to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies trust our all-in-one platform to get paid, manage money and grow on their terms. Simple, scalable and built with real businesses in mind.

We're one of Europe's fastest-growing fintechs, with 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations. Our people make this growth possible. We move fast, build with purpose and care deeply about our customers. Whether you're solving problems, building market-leading products or exploring how AI can make work smarter, you'll have the freedom to create and the trust to deliver.

If you're ready to grow, shape the future of fintech and join an ambitious, high-performing team, this is the place for you.

Your impact

Cards is one of the most strategically important products at Mollie. It is the primary payment method operating at a global scale and the central enabler for Mollie to serve larger, more sophisticated merchants. As the accountable lead for online cards acceptance, you will own one of the highest net revenue-generating areas in the business, and your work will directly shape Mollie's ability to compete for and retain enterprise and mid-market merchants.

As the Head of Product for Cards Acquiring, you will own the end-to-end product strategy and execution for one of the most critical payment methods. You will bridge the gap between heavy technical infrastructure and high-impact commercial enablement. Leading a cross-functional team of around 20 people that includes product delivery managers, a product partnership person, a dedicated data person, and a PMM, you will scale Mollie’s cards capabilities beyond Europe, unlock new merchant categories, and ensure our proposition wins the hearts of highly sophisticated merchants. You will also work directly with payment schemes and external partners, making decisions that influence both the product roadmap and Mollie's broader positioning in the market.

The cards domain is expected to become an increasingly primary driver of Mollie's growth over time, with the potential for the online and in-person card acceptance platforms to converge and expand the scope of this role significantly. If you want to own something that matters at a company that is moving fast in the right direction, this is it.

What you'll ship

  • End-to-end product ownership: own the full cards acceptance product lifecycle—from deep technical infrastructure and processing stability to commercial enablement.

  • Go-To-Market & commercial enablement: lead the GTM strategy for new card features in tight lockstep with Product Marketing (PMM) and Commercial teams. You'll translate complex technical capabilities into crystal-clear value propositions that our sales teams can run with.

  • Global scale: drive the geographic expansion of our cards product, building out capabilities beyond Europe to support Mollie’s international growth.

  • Portfolio optimisation: Identify untapped merchant vertical opportunities and make data-driven decisions to maximise net revenue across the entire cards portfolio.

  • Team Leadership: Manage, coach, and scale a high-performing product team.

What You’ll Bring

  • Commercial & GTM Strategy: A proven track record of launching successful financial/payment products. You know how to price, position, and package features alongside PMM to win market share.

  • Partnership acumen: deep understanding of direct vs. indirect relationship strategies in the payments ecosystem and their respective commercial implications.
